problems.text: A sprinter's top speed is 36 km/h. Express this speed in m/s.
Use dimensional analysis to check whether the expression v = sqrt(2gh) has units of speed, then convert 55 mi/h to meters per second.
Vector A has magnitude 12 m and points 35° north of east. Find its x and y components.
Two displacement vectors, 5.0 m east and 8.0 m north, are added. Find the magnitude and direction of the resultant.
A jet accelerates uniformly from rest to 80 m/s over a 1.2 km runway. What is its acceleration?
A truck moving at 25 m/s decelerates at 4.0 m/s^2. How long does it take to stop, and how far does it travel?
A wrench is dropped from a scaffold 45 m above the ground. How fast is it moving just before it hits?
A ball is thrown straight up at 14 m/s. How high does it rise, and when does it return to the thrower's hand? Ignore air resistance.
The velocity–time graph of a cart is a straight line from 2 m/s at t = 0 to 10 m/s at t = 4 s. Use the area under the graph to find the displacement.
From the position–time graph shown, determine the slope between t = 1 s and t = 3 s. What does the slope represent?
A particle's position is x(t) = 4t^3 − 2t^2 + 5 (x in m, t in s). Find its instantaneous velocity and acceleration at t = 2 s.
The velocity of an object is v(t) = 6t − t^2 m/s. Find its displacement between t = 0 and t = 3 s.
A soccer ball is kicked at 22 m/s at 40° above the horizontal. Find its maximum height and horizontal range on level ground.
A stone is thrown horizontally at 9.0 m/s from the top of a 25 m cliff. How far from the base of the cliff does it land?
A boat heads straight across a 120 m wide river at 4.0 m/s relative to the water. The current flows at 1.5 m/s. How far downstream does it land?
A plane flies north at 250 km/h relative to the air while a wind blows east at 60 km/h. Find its velocity relative to the ground.
A car travels around a circular track of radius 80 m at a constant speed of 20 m/s. What is its centripetal acceleration?
A centrifuge spins at 3000 rpm with a radius of 12 cm. Find the speed of a sample at the edge and its acceleration.
A net force of 120 N acts on a 30 kg crate on a frictionless floor. What is the crate's acceleration?
Two forces act on a 4.0 kg object: 10 N east and 6 N west. Find the object's acceleration using Newton's second law.
A 6.0 kg box slides down a frictionless incline tilted at 30°. Find its acceleration and the normal force.
What angle of ramp gives a frictionless cart an acceleration of 3.0 m/s^2 down the slope?
In an Atwood machine, masses of 3.0 kg and 5.0 kg hang over a light frictionless pulley. Find the acceleration and the tension in the string.
A 2.0 kg block on a frictionless table is tied by a rope over a pulley to a hanging 1.0 kg mass. Find the tension.
A 40 kg crate rests on a floor with coefficient of static friction 0.45. What horizontal push is needed to start it moving?
A hockey puck slides on rough ice with μk = 0.08. If it starts at 12 m/s, how far does it go before stopping?
A 70 kg person stands on a scale in an elevator accelerating upward at 1.5 m/s^2. What does the scale read?
While an elevator slows down on its way up, will a bathroom scale inside read more or less than your weight? Compute the reading for a 55 kg student if the deceleration is 2.0 m/s^2.
A 1500 kg car rounds a flat curve of radius 60 m. The coefficient of static friction is 0.7. What is the maximum speed before it skids?
A curve of radius 150 m is banked for a design speed of 25 m/s with no friction needed. What is the banking angle?
A skydiver of mass 80 kg falls with drag force F = bv^2, where b = 0.25 kg/m. What is her terminal velocity?
A raindrop reaches terminal speed when air resistance balances its weight. If the drag is proportional to speed, find how long it takes to reach half the terminal speed.
A small mass hangs from the ceiling of a bus accelerating at 2.0 m/s^2. What angle does the string make with the vertical, as seen by a passenger?
In the accelerating frame of a truck, a crate feels a fictitious force. Find the pseudo-force on a 20 kg crate when the truck accelerates at 3 m/s^2.
A worker pulls a sled 25 m with a rope at 30° above the horizontal and a tension of 80 N. How much work does the rope do?
How much work is done lifting a 12 kg box straight up 1.8 m at constant speed? Give the answer in joules.
A spring with k = 300 N/m is stretched from its natural length by 0.12 m. How much work is done on the spring?
A force F(x) = 5x^2 N acts along the x-axis. Find the work done as the object moves from x = 0 to x = 3 m.
A net force does 450 J of work on a 3.0 kg ball initially at rest. Use the work–energy theorem to find its final speed.
A 1200 kg car slows from 30 m/s to 10 m/s. How much net work was done on it? What is the change in kinetic energy?
A roller coaster car starts from rest at the top of a 35 m hill. Ignoring friction, how fast is it moving at the bottom?
A pendulum bob is released from a height of 0.40 m above its lowest point. Use conservation of mechanical energy to find its speed at the bottom.
A 5.0 kg block slides down a 4.0 m ramp and arrives at the bottom with less speed than expected. If 60 J of thermal energy was produced, how fast is it moving?
A sled loses energy to friction as it crosses a rough patch. How much mechanical energy is dissipated if its speed drops from 8 m/s to 5 m/s? The sled's mass is 20 kg.
An elevator motor lifts 800 kg at 2.5 m/s. What power does it deliver, in kW?
A cyclist produces 250 W while riding at constant speed against a 20 N resistive force. How fast is she riding? Also express the power in horsepower.
A 0.058 kg tennis ball arrives at 30 m/s and leaves the racket at 40 m/s in the opposite direction. The contact lasts 5.0 ms. Find the average force.
What impulse (in N·s) is delivered to a 0.4 kg ball that bounces off a wall, reversing its 6 m/s velocity?
A 60 kg skater at rest throws a 5.0 kg ball forward at 12 m/s. What is the skater's recoil speed?
A 2.0 kg firecracker at rest explodes into two pieces. One piece of 0.8 kg moves at 15 m/s. How fast does the other move? Use conservation of momentum.
A 1000 kg car moving at 20 m/s rear-ends a 1500 kg car at rest, and they stick together. What is their speed after the collision?
A 10 g bullet embeds in a 2.0 kg wooden block hanging from strings (a ballistic pendulum). The block rises 5.0 cm. Find the bullet's speed.
A 0.5 kg cart moving at 4 m/s makes an elastic head-on collision with a stationary 1.5 kg cart. Find both velocities afterward.
In a perfectly elastic collision, a billiard ball hits an identical ball at rest head-on. What are the final velocities?
A 3 kg puck moving east at 5 m/s collides with a 2 kg puck moving north at 4 m/s. They stick. Find the magnitude and direction of the final velocity.
After a glancing collision, one ball moves at 30° above the x-axis. Using momentum components, find the speed of the second ball.
Masses of 2 kg, 3 kg and 5 kg sit at x = 0, 4 m and 6 m. Locate the center of mass of the system.
A thin rod of length 2 m has linear density λ(x) = 3 + x kg/m. Find the location of its center of mass.
A rocket ejects exhaust at 2500 m/s relative to the rocket and burns fuel until its mass drops from 1200 kg to 700 kg. Find its change in speed.
What thrust does a rocket engine produce if it expels 15 kg of fuel per second at an exhaust speed of 3000 m/s?
A wheel speeds up from 2.0 rad/s to 14 rad/s in 4.0 s. What is its angular acceleration, and how many revolutions does it make?
A fan spinning at 900 rpm is switched off and stops after 12 s. Find the angular deceleration in rad/s^2.
Find the moment of inertia of a 2.0 kg uniform rod 1.2 m long about an axis through one end. Use the parallel-axis theorem.
Three point masses of 1 kg each sit at the corners of an equilateral triangle of side 0.5 m. Find the rotational inertia about an axis through one corner.
A mechanic applies 60 N to a wrench 0.25 m long at 70° to the handle. What torque does she apply?
A 4.0 N·m torque acts on a disk with I = 0.8 kg·m^2. What is the disk's angular acceleration?
A flywheel with I = 12 kg·m^2 spins at 300 rad/s. How much rotational kinetic energy does it store?
A solid cylinder of mass 5 kg and radius 0.2 m spins at 40 rad/s. Find its rotational kinetic energy.
A solid sphere rolls without slipping down a 2.0 m high incline from rest. Find its speed at the bottom.
A hoop and a disk roll down the same ramp. Which one reaches the bottom first, and what is the disk's speed if the ramp is 1.5 m tall?
A figure skater spinning at 2.0 rev/s pulls in her arms, reducing her moment of inertia from 3.5 to 1.4 kg·m^2. What is her new spin rate?
A child of mass 25 kg jumps onto the edge of a merry-go-round turntable (I = 200 kg·m^2, R = 2 m) spinning at 1.0 rad/s. Find the new angular velocity.
A uniform 6 m plank weighing 300 N rests on supports at its ends. A 500 N person stands 2 m from the left end. Find the force from each support.
A seesaw is balanced with a 30 kg child 1.5 m from the pivot. Where must a 45 kg child sit for equilibrium?
A 5.0 m ladder of mass 12 kg leans against a frictionless wall at 60° to the ground. What minimum coefficient of friction at the floor keeps it from slipping?
A horizontal boom of length 3 m is hinged at a wall and held by a cable at 40°. A 200 N sign hangs from its end. Find the cable tension.
Find the gravitational force between two 800 kg satellites 4.0 m apart. Use G = 6.67 × 10^-11 N·m^2/kg^2.
What is the gravitational acceleration at the surface of a planet with twice Earth's mass and 1.5 times its radius?
A satellite orbits Earth at an altitude of 400 km. Find its orbital speed and period.
Use Kepler's third law: a moon orbits a planet with a period of 3.2 days at a radius of 2.1 × 10^8 m. Find the planet's mass.
Calculate the escape speed from the surface of the Moon (M = 7.35 × 10^22 kg, R = 1.74 × 10^6 m).
How much energy is needed to move a 500 kg probe from Earth's surface to a very large distance? Use gravitational potential energy U = −GMm/r.
A 0.25 kg mass on a spring with k = 40 N/m oscillates horizontally. Find the period and frequency of the motion.
A block on a spring undergoes simple harmonic motion with amplitude 5 cm and frequency 2 Hz. What is its maximum speed?
What length should a simple pendulum have to swing with a period of exactly 2.0 s?
A pendulum 0.80 m long is taken to a planet where g = 3.7 m/s^2. What is its period there?
A mass–spring system has k = 200 N/m and amplitude 0.10 m. Find the total mechanical energy and the speed when x = 0.06 m, if m = 0.5 kg.
In simple harmonic motion, at what displacement (as a fraction of the amplitude) is the kinetic energy equal to the potential energy?
A uniform meter stick swings from a pivot at one end. Treat it as a physical pendulum and find its period of small oscillations.
A disk of radius 0.3 m pivots about a point on its rim. Find the period of small oscillations of this physical pendulum.
What is the gauge pressure at a depth of 12 m in fresh water? Give the absolute pressure too.
A hydraulic lift has pistons of area 0.02 m^2 and 0.5 m^2. What force on the small piston lifts a 1200 kg car?
A 0.6 kg block of wood floats in water with 70% of its volume submerged. Find the buoyant force and the wood's density.
A metal sample weighs 5.0 N in air and 3.2 N when fully submerged in water. Using Archimedes' principle, find its density.
Water flows through a pipe that narrows from 6 cm to 3 cm in diameter. If the speed in the wide section is 1.5 m/s, find the speed in the narrow part.
Use Bernoulli's equation to find the speed of water leaving a small hole 2.5 m below the surface of an open tank.

sheets.title: Ph 112 Homework 4
sheets.text:
Ph 112 — Homework 4: Newton's Laws
Name ____________________ Date __________
1. A 25 kg crate is pushed across a floor by a 120 N horizontal force. The coefficient of kinetic friction is 0.30. Find the crate's acceleration.
2. A 3.0 kg block slides down a frictionless ramp inclined at 35°. How long does it take to slide 2.0 m from rest?
3) Two blocks, 4 kg and 6 kg, are connected by a string over a frictionless pulley (an Atwood machine).
(a) Draw free-body diagrams for each block.
(b) Find the tension in the string.
4. Sketch the forces acting on a car rounding a banked curve.
5. A 900 kg car takes a flat curve of radius 40 m at 15 m/s. What friction force is required?

sheets.title: Physics 1 Problem Set 7
sheets.text:
Physics 1 — Problem Set 7
Energy and Momentum
Problem 1 A 2.0 kg ball is dropped from 10 m. Using conservation of energy, find its speed just before impact.
Problem 2 How much power must a motor supply to lift a 300 kg load 12 m in 20 s?
Problem 3 A 1200 kg truck at 15 m/s collides with a 900 kg car at rest; they stick together. Find their common velocity.
Problem 4 A 0.2 kg ball hits a wall at 8 m/s and rebounds at 6 m/s. The contact time is 0.02 s. Find the average force from the wall.
Problem 5 Explain in your own words why momentum is conserved in an isolated system.

sheets.title: Mechanics Quiz 3
sheets.text:
Mechanics — Quiz 3 Review
1. A merry-go-round with I = 250 kg m^2 spins at 0.8 rad/s. A 40 kg child steps on at r = 1.5 m. Find the new angular velocity.
2. A torque of 12 N·m is applied to a wheel with moment of inertia 3 kg·m^2. What is its angular acceleration?
3. A 0.5 kg mass on a spring (k = 50 N/m) is pulled 10 cm from equilibrium and released. Find the period.
4. A satellite orbits 300 km above the Earth's surface. What is its orbital period?
5. A stone is thrown horizontally at 15 m/s from a 20 m tall building. Where does it land?
